meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Activity 5 of 9 (quiz/game): Timed Try 2 - Usage Debates and Style Guides
meta.title: Timed Try 2: Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A school guide says to use that for defining clauses that identify a specific group. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Students that attend the workshop earn extra credit.
Students who attend the workshop earn extra credit.
Students that attends the workshop earns extra credit.
Students whom attends the workshop earn extra credit.
questions.explanation: The clause that attend the workshop identifies the students who qualify, so it is a defining clause introduced by that.

questions.prompt: A transit guide requires the 24-hour clock and prohibits a.m. and p.m. after the time. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The bus leaves at 19:45 from the north platform.
The bus leaves at 7:45 p.m. from the north platform.
The bus leaves at 7:45 a.m. from the north platform.
The bus leaves at 19:45 p.m. from the north platform.
questions.explanation: The 24-hour system represents 7:45 p.m. as 19:45 and does not add a.m. or p.m.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use criterion for one standard and criteria for several standards. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The rubric includes one criterias for evaluating a project.
The rubric includes three criterions for evaluating a project.
The rubric includes three criteria for evaluating a project.
The rubric includes one criteria for evaluating a project.
questions.explanation: Because the rubric includes several standards, the plural noun criteria is correct in The rubric includes three criteria for evaluating a project.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to form the possessive of a plural noun ending in s by adding an apostrophe after the s. Which phrase follows the rule?
choices: the coach's travel bags
the coaches's travel bags
the coaches' travel bags
the coaches travel bags
questions.explanation: The plural noun coaches takes an apostrophe after the s to show possession in the phrase coaches' travel bags.

questions.prompt: A travel publication's style guide says to use different from rather than different than when comparing two things. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: This route is different from the route we took yesterday.
This route is different than the route we took yesterday.
This route is different to the route we took yesterday.
This route is different of the route we took yesterday.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses different from, the comparison phrase required by the publication's style guide.

questions.prompt: A committee's style guide says to use comprise directly with its object, without of or the passive construction is comprised of. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The review committee comprises 12 members.
The review committee comprises of 12 members.
The review committee is comprised of 12 members.
The review committee comprises 12 of members.
questions.explanation: The sentence places the object members directly after comprises and avoids both prohibited constructions.
questions.skill: Following a guide on verb usage

questions.prompt: A publication's style guide says to use whose for possession and who's for the contraction of who is. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The writer who latest novel received an award spoke to students.
The writer whose latest novel received an award spoke to students.
The writer who's latest novel received an award spoke to students.
The writer whom latest novel received an award spoke to students.
questions.explanation: Whose shows that the latest novel belongs to the writer, which is the possessive use required by the guide.
questions.skill: Distinguishing whose from who's and similar forms

questions.prompt: A magazine's style guide requires a single em dash with no spaces on either side. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The train arrived at noon--the visitors were ready.
The train arrived at noon — the visitors were ready.
The train arrived at noon - the visitors were ready.
The train arrived at noon—the visitors were ready.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses one em dash without spaces on either side, matching the magazine's rule.

questions.prompt: A nonprofit's guide says to use ensure for making certain, assure for reassuring someone, and insure for providing financial protection. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The coordinator will assure that the welcome desk has enough copies.
The coordinator will insure that the welcome desk has enough copies.
The coordinator will ensure that the welcome desk has enough copies.
The coordinator will assert that the welcome desk has enough copies.
questions.explanation: Ensure means to make certain, which matches the coordinator's goal of confirming that the welcome desk has enough copies.

questions.prompt: A research organization's style guide says to treat data as a plural noun. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The data shows a consistent pattern.
The data show a consistent pattern.
The datum show a consistent pattern.
The datas show a consistent pattern.
questions.explanation: Treating data as plural requires the plural verb show in The data show a consistent pattern.

questions.prompt: A newspaper's style guide says to use toward rather than towards. What should a writer do in an article for the newspaper?
choices: Alternate between toward and towards from one paragraph to the next
Use towards rather than toward in the article
Use toward rather than towards in the article
Replace both forms with in the direction of throughout the article
questions.explanation: Following the stated house style means using toward rather than towards in the newspaper's copy.

questions.prompt: A research guide says imply means to suggest and infer means to reach a conclusion from evidence. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The data imply a trend, and readers can imply the cause.
The data infer a trend, and readers can imply the cause.
The data imply a trend, and readers can infer the cause.
The data infer a trend, and readers can infer the cause.
questions.explanation: The data suggest a trend through implication, while readers infer the cause by drawing a conclusion from the evidence.

questions.prompt: A rescue center's style guide says to use lay for put or rest and lie for recline. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The tired cat lay on the blanket yesterday.
The tired cat laid on the blanket yesterday.
The tired cat lie on the blanket yesterday.
The tired cat lain on the blanket yesterday.
questions.explanation: The past-tense form of lie is lay, so the sentence correctly describes the cat resting on the blanket.
questions.skill: Distinguishing lay and lie in a specified tense

questions.prompt: A school guide says principal means a leader or chief, while principle means a basic rule or belief. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The principal explained the school's important principal to the students.
The principle explained the school's important principal to the students.
The principle explained the school's important principle to the students.
The principal explained the school's important principle to the students.
questions.explanation: The principal is the school leader who explains the school's important principle, which is a basic rule or belief.

questions.prompt: A British publisher's style guide uses storeys for floors of a building and stories for floors of a ship. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The apartment has three stories, and the ship has five storeys.
The apartment has three stories, and the ship has five stories.
The apartment has three storeys, and the ship has five storeys.
The apartment has three storeys, and the ship has five stories.
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly uses storeys for the apartment's floors and stories for the ship's floors.

questions.prompt: In these sentences, affect is intended to mean influence, and effect is intended to mean a result. Which sentence uses both words correctly?
choices: The delay may effect attendance, and missed classes may have an affect on grades.
The delay may affect attendance, and missed classes may have an effect on grades.
The delay may affect attendance, and missed classes may have an affect on grades.
The delay may effect attendance, and missed classes may have an effect on grades.
questions.explanation: Affect functions as the verb meaning influence, while effect functions as the noun meaning a result.

questions.prompt: A magazine's style guide says book titles should be italicized and article titles should be placed in quotation marks. The sentence names the book The Glass Harbor and the article Inside the Harbor. Which formatting choice follows the guide?
choices: Set The Glass Harbor in bold and Inside the Harbor in italics.
Set The Glass Harbor in quotation marks and Inside the Harbor in italics.
Set The Glass Harbor in italics and Inside the Harbor in quotation marks.
Set both titles in italics and capitalize every word in them.
questions.explanation: This formats the book title in italics and the article title in quotation marks, exactly as the magazine's guide requires.

questions.prompt: A newsletter guide requires a semicolon to join two closely related independent clauses. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The first round ended; the judges announced the results immediately.
The first round ended, the judges announced the results immediately.
The first round ended: the judges announced the results immediately.
The first round ended the judges announced the results immediately.
questions.explanation: The semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses that express closely related ideas.
questions.skill: Using a semicolon between independent clauses

questions.prompt: Which guideline most clearly states a standard house rule for compound modifiers?
choices: Replace a hyphen in a compound modifier with a space whenever possible
Use a hyphen only when a compound modifier comes after the noun it modifies
Leave every compound modifier unhyphenated when it appears before a noun
Use a hyphen when a compound modifier comes before the noun it modifies
questions.explanation: A compound modifier that comes before the noun it modifies is normally joined with hyphens.

questions.prompt: A newspaper's guide requires one l in both traveling and canceled. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The traveling team cancelled its game because of rain.
The traveling team canceled its game because of rain.
The cancelled traveling team rescheduled its game.
The traveled team canceled its game before the storm arrived.
questions.explanation: Traveling and canceled each use one l, exactly as the guide requires.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly follows the standard distinction between fewer and less and also keeps the verb in agreement with the subject?
choices: Less than 20 tickets is remaining.
Less than 20 tickets remain.
Fewer than 20 tickets remains.
Fewer than 20 tickets remain.
questions.explanation: Fewer is used with the countable noun tickets, and the plural subject requires the verb remain.

questions.prompt: Which sentence meets a nonprofit guide that requires whom for a person functioning as the object of a preposition?
choices: Who should I send the completed forms to?
To who should I send the completed forms?
To whom should I send the completed forms?
To whom should I sent the completed forms?
questions.explanation: Because whom is the object of the preposition to, the opening phrase should read To whom.

questions.prompt: A nonprofit's style guide says to write percentages as numerals followed by the percent sign, with no space. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Only twelve percent of the forms were returned by Friday.
Only 12% of the forms were returned by Friday.
Only 12 percent of the forms were returned by Friday.
Only 12 % of the forms were returned by Friday.
questions.explanation: This sentence correctly expresses the percentage as the numeral 12 followed immediately by the percent sign.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use farther for physical distance and further for an additional amount or degree. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The trail is further from the school, and the extra reading requires further study.
The trail is further from the school, and the extra reading requires farther study.
The trail is farther from the school, and the extra reading requires farther study.
The trail is farther from the school, and the extra reading requires further study.
questions.explanation: Farther correctly describes the trail's physical distance from the school, while further describes the additional amount of study required.

questions.prompt: A nonprofit's guide says to write an organization's full name followed by its abbreviation in parentheses at first mention and use the abbreviation afterward. Which paragraph follows the guide?
choices: The National Association of Environmental Educators (NAEE) published a guide. The NAEE shared it with local schools.
The National Association of Environmental Educators (NAEE) published a guide. The organization shared it with local schools.
The National Association of Environmental Educators (NAEE) published a guide. The National Association of Environmental Educators shared it with local schools.
The NAEE published a guide. The National Association of Environmental Educators shared it with local schools.
questions.explanation: This paragraph gives the organization's full name with its abbreviation at first mention and uses the abbreviation in the next sentence.

questions.prompt: A school style guide says to use a singular verb after the phrase a couple of. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: A couple of forms remain on the desk.
A couple of form remains on the desk.
A couple of form remain on the desk.
A couple of forms remains on the desk.
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly treats a couple of as the singular subject and uses the singular verb remains.

questions.prompt: A school guide says complement means something that completes or agrees with something, while compliment means praise. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The blue scarf compliments her coat, and the teacher gave her a complement.
The blue scarf complements her coat, and the teacher gave her a compliment.
The blue scarf compliments her coat, and the teacher gave her a compliment.
The blue scarf complements her coat, and the teacher gave her a complement.
questions.explanation: The scarf complements the coat by completing its appearance, and the compliment expresses the teacher's praise.

questions.prompt: A shelter's style guide says to use stationary for fixed in one place and stationery for writing supplies. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The wheels remain stationery while the stationery is sorted.
The wheels remain stationary while the stationary is sorted.
The wheels remain stationery while the stationary is sorted.
The wheels remain stationary while the stationery is sorted.
questions.explanation: The wheels are stationary because they remain fixed in place, while the paper and other writing materials are stationery.
questions.skill: Applying a stationary and stationery style rule

questions.prompt: Why can a style guide help resolve a disputed usage within a publication?
choices: A single convention makes one variant correct in every English-speaking community.
A single convention helps writers and editors apply the same rule consistently.
A single convention removes the need to consider the publication's audience.
A single convention prevents style guides from recording preferred practices.
questions.explanation: A house convention gives writers and editors one consistent rule to apply.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why reputable style guides sometimes recommend different usages?
choices: Usage changes over time, but every style guide must reach the same final decision
Usage changes over time, and different audiences may favor different conventions
Most disputed usages are settled permanently by the oldest surviving rules
All disputed usages become incorrect once a newer form appears
questions.explanation: Style guides reflect both changing language and the needs of their particular audiences, so their recommendations can differ.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of a publication's style guide?
choices: To record the publication's preferred conventions for language and formatting
To prove that every disputed usage is grammatically correct
To replace dictionaries and other grammar references
To show which rules every English speaker has always followed
questions.explanation: A style guide establishes the publication's preferred conventions so writers and editors can apply them consistently.
questions.skill: Identifying the purpose of a style guide

questions.prompt: A publisher's style guide says to use afterwards for the adverb meaning later and afterwords for remarks printed at the end of a book. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: We can meet afterwords, and the afterwards discuss the new edition.
We can meet afterwards, and the afterwords discuss the new edition.
We can meet afterwards, and the afterwards discuss the new edition.
We can meet afterwords, and the afterwords discuss the new edition.
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly uses afterwards to mean later and afterwords to refer to the closing remarks in a book.
questions.skill: Distinguishing words with different parts of speech

questions.prompt: A school style guide says to spell out numbers from zero through nine, use numerals for 10 and above, and use numerals for ages and percentages. Which sentence follows all three rules?
choices: The club has 12 members; 25 percent joined last year, and the youngest member is eight years old.
The club has 12 members; twenty-five percent joined last year, and the youngest member is 8 years old.
The club has 12 members; 25 percent joined last year, and the youngest member is 8 years old.
The club has twelve members; twenty-five percent joined last year, and the youngest member is eight years old.
questions.explanation: This option uses numerals for 12 and 25 and for the age 8, exactly as the guide requires.

questions.prompt: Under a newsletter rule requiring a comma after an introductory prepositional phrase of three or more words, which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: After the opening ceremony the finalists met the judges.
After the opening ceremony, the finalists met the judges.
After the opening ceremony the finalists, met the judges.
After the opening ceremony, the finalists, met the judges.
questions.explanation: The introductory phrase After the opening ceremony is followed by the required comma.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires an en dash without spaces for a range of page numbers. Which range is formatted correctly?
choices: Pages 20-35
Pages 20 – 35
Pages 20—35
Pages 20–35
questions.explanation: The en dash joins 20 and 35 directly without spaces, as the style guide requires.
questions.skill: Formatting numerical ranges with an en dash

questions.prompt: A style guide says that a singular name ending in s takes an apostrophe followed by s to show possession. Which phrase follows the rule?
choices: the bosses's recommendation
the boss' recommendation
the bosses' recommendation
the boss's recommendation
questions.explanation: The boss is singular and ends in s, so the guide's rule calls for boss's.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use among for more than two people or things and between for exactly two. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The decision was discussed between the three finalists.
The decision was discussed between the four finalists.
The decision was discussed among the two finalists.
The decision was discussed among the four finalists.
questions.explanation: Among correctly takes the group of four finalists because the group contains more than two members.

questions.prompt: A community newspaper's style guide says to use in spite of, followed by a comma, to introduce a concession. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: In spite of the rain the outdoor concert began on time.
Despite of the rain, the outdoor concert began on time.
In spite of the rain, the outdoor concert began on time.
Despite the rain, the outdoor concert began on time.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses the required phrase in spite of and correctly sets off the introductory phrase with a comma.

questions.prompt: A tennis club's style guide says to spell the noun practice with a c and the verb practise with an s. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The team's regular practise will help them practice serves.
The team's regular practice will help them practise serves.
The team's regular practice will help them practice serves.
The team's regular practise will help them practise serves.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses practice as a noun and practise as a verb, matching the club's stated spellings.

questions.prompt: A school style guide says to use it's for it is and its for possession. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The committee postponed it's vote because it needed more time.
The committee postponed its vote because it's needed more time.
The committee postponed its vote because it needed more time.
The committee postponed it's vote because it's needed more time.
questions.explanation: Here its shows possession of the vote, while it's stands for it is in the because clause.
questions.skill: Distinguishing possessive its from the contraction it's

questions.prompt: A magazine's style guide requires the serial comma. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: The package contains a pen, a notebook, and a folder.
The package contains a pen a notebook and a folder.
The package contains a pen; a notebook; and a folder.
The package contains a pen: a notebook and a folder.
questions.explanation: The required serial comma appears before and in a list of three items.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to use third-person singular they, their, and them when a person's pronouns are not stated. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The new student forgot to bring his or her permission form.
The new student forgot to bring their permission form.
The new student forgot to bring him or her permission form.
The new student forgot to bring theirself permission form.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses third-person singular agreement with the subject and their as the possessive, matching the guide's singular-they pattern.

questions.prompt: Which phrase correctly shows that one student owns the cafeteria?
choices: the student's cafeteria
the students' cafeteria
the students cafeteria
the student cafeteria's
questions.explanation: The singular possessive student's shows that the cafeteria belongs to one student.

questions.prompt: A newspaper's style guide says to write dates with the month first, followed by the day, and to omit an ordinal suffix. Which date follows the rule?
choices: July 4
July 4th
4 July
the 4th of July
questions.explanation: The date July 4 places the month first and omits the ordinal suffix as the style guide requires.

questions.prompt: A newsletter guide says altogether means entirely or in total, while all together means in one group. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The judges considered the proposal altogether, and the team stood all together near the door.
The judges considered the proposal all together, and the team stood altogether near the door.
The judges considered the proposal altogether, and the team stood altogether near the door.
The judges considered the proposal all together, and the team stood all together near the door.
questions.explanation: The judges considered the proposal in total, while the team stood all together as a group near the door.

questions.prompt: A style guide says to begin a sentence with Although and set off the rest of the dependent clause with a comma. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: Although the buses were late, the class began on time.
Although, the buses were late, the class began on time.
Although the buses were late the class began on time.
Although the buses were late; the class began on time.
questions.explanation: This sentence places the comma correctly after the introductory dependent clause beginning with Although.

questions.prompt: A community newspaper's style guide says to refer to the group as people with visual impairments, not as the visually impaired. Which sentence follows the guide exactly?
choices: Visually impaired people attended the evening workshop.
The visually impaired attended the evening workshop.
People with visual impairments attended the evening workshop.
People with blindness attended the evening workshop.
questions.explanation: This uses the exact phrase people with visual impairments that the newspaper's style guide requires.

questions.prompt: A publication's style guide does not address whether to use who or that to introduce a defining clause. What is the best next step for a writer?
choices: Choose whichever form feels more familiar and proceed
Ask the editor which form the publication wants
Assume the older form is correct because it has existed longer
Use both forms together so the sentence remains consistent
questions.explanation: When the guide is silent on a disputed usage, asking the editor is the best way to identify the publication's chosen convention.

questions.prompt: A newsletter's style guide says to treat each as the singular subject in a sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Each of the volunteers are completing the training.
Each of the volunteers have completed the training.
Each of the volunteer have completed the training.
Each of the volunteers has completed the training.
questions.explanation: Because the guide treats each as singular, it takes the singular verb has in Each of the volunteers has completed the training.

questions.prompt: A magazine's guide says to use e.g. followed by a comma when introducing an example within a sentence. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: Some studies, i.e., this one, show a clear pattern.
Some studies, e.g. this one, show a clear pattern.
Some studies, e.g., this one, show a clear pattern.
Some studies, e.g. those by Rao, show a clear pattern.
questions.explanation: The abbreviation e.g. introduces an example and is followed by the required comma.

kept.explanation: Fewer is used with the countable noun tickets, and the plural subject requires the verb remain.

The trail is farther from the school, and the extra reading requires farther study.
